newsitem.title: GERMANY: Holzmann offsets charges with assets, revaluations.
newsitem.headline: Holzmann offsets charges with assets, revaluations.

text.p: German construction group Philipp Holzmann said on Thursday it offset 1996 charges of just over one billion marks with a number of items including asset sales and a revaluation of its work in progress.

Holzmann chief financial officer Rainer Klee told a news briefing that sales of assets -- such as the group's head office in a lease-back deal -- had boosted its profit-and-loss account by 300.4 million marks.
A further 290.4 million marks came in as a result of sales of apartments that the group had on its books.
The largest surplus came however from a revaluation of both reserves the group is planning to sell and of the worth to the company of work for which it had not yet billed.
Such revalutions all together amounted to a gain of 431.7 million marks at the construction group, Klee said.

Holzmann noted in its newly-published 1996 annual report that an "appropriate part" of management costs associated with unfinished or unbilled-for projects had been included within capitalised production costs.
This allows them to be recognised as an asset.
Klee said the revaluation was "perfectly legal" and the company had already gained the approval of its auditors for the move.

The new accounting measures allowed Holzmann to report a break-even result for the 1996 year. At the operating level, a 300 million mark loss was made, equivalent to a 60 to 70 mark loss per share according to the DVFA German accounting standard.

The 1.044 billion marks of charges booked by Holzmann in 1996 included 464.7 million marks related to the restructuring and revaluation of ongoing project business, 288.1 million marks of write-offs on funding advanced to subsidiaries and a further 178.1 million in write-offs on the book values of certain of its divisions.
